messages:
Sophia: Heads-up — promote is blocked. Staging e2e failing consistently on auth-service tests since 12:03UTC. First observed during canary run 6800123400. Logs show 401s when hitting token refresh endpoint.

Mike: Can you paste the failing test output? Flaky or deterministic? :eyes:

Sophia: paste of the failing snippet below:
```
FAIL tests/integration/test_auth_refresh.py::test_refresh_token_rotation
E   AssertionError: expected 200 but got 401
E   Request: POST /internal/auth/refresh - body={"refresh_token": "***"}
E   Response headers: {"x-cache-status": "HIT", "x-cache-ttl": "-1"}
```

Jia: x-cache-ttl -1 sounds like a stale cache entry being returned by the remote fixture cache. We had a deployment earlier that changed token format; if CI cache returned an old fixture it would 401.

Oliver: Is this the same failure as yesterday? We had a transient auth token mismatch but only 1/20 runs. This looks reproducible for this canary.

Sophia: Reproducible ~5/5 in this run. Re-ran the job with cache disabled: `CI_CACHE=off ./ci/run-staging-e2e.sh` -> all tests passed. So cache appears to be the culprit.

deploy-bot: Promotion blocked by failing checks: `staging-e2e` (job id 6800123501). Automatic rollback is OFF for this pipeline. :no_entry_sign:

Mike: OK. Two options: 1) pin to last-good image (sha: sha256:aa11bb22) and manual promote, 2) rollback the change that introduced token format. Which is faster for the release window?

Jia: Pinning image is fastest. We should also invalidate the remote cache and re-run the canary to confirm. I can trigger cache eviction script: `scripts/ci/invalidate-fixtures --prefix=auth-service/staging` but it can take ~2-3m.

Oliver: If pin is chosen we need release note and a follow-up bug to unpin and fix the cache TTL. Also schedule the unpin outside the change window. Anyone from platform oncall?

Sophia: Oncall SRE is Mike today. Mike — do you approve pin + manual promote while we investigate cache TTL change?

Mike: Approve pin+promote. I'll run the eviction after we pin. Steps I will take now:
1) tag last-good: `deploybot promote --image=sha256:aa11bb22 --env=staging --manual`
2) run `scripts/ci/invalidate-fixtures --prefix=auth-service/staging`
3) re-run canary smoke `./ci/retry-job 6800123501`

Jia: I'll also open a tracking issue and add a quick smoke test to fail CI if cache returns TTL < 0.

deploy-bot: Manual promote initiated by Mike. Promotion status: queued -> in-progress.

ci-bot: Staging canary replaced with image sha256:aa11bb22 by manual promote (link: https://ci.example.com/job/6800123501).

Sophia: Re-run result: canary smoke passed after cache eviction. All staging e2e green.

Oliver: Great. We'll ship the pinned image for this release and include in release notes: "Pinned auth-service to last-good image due to remote fixture cache TTL regression; follow-up unpin scheduled post-change-window." Add an item in release-notes/ to flag for QA.

Mike: After release, we'll plan a small maintenance window to fix cache TTL handling and unpin. Creating the follow-up ticket now: RD-2345.

Jia: Ticket RD-2345 created, assigned to Platform -> priority P1 for post-release. I'll attach logs and the `x-cache-ttl` evidence.

Sophia: Thanks team. :thumbsup: We're unblocked for the release window.

Oliver: Note for postmortem: add a short blurb on 'CI fixture caches must honor TTL and be invalidatable per-service' and link to RD-2345.

Mike: Will follow up with an ops runbook for manual cache eviction so oncall can act faster next time.

deploy-bot: Promotion completed. Release window proceed allowed. :tada:
